volunteer.organization: Buddy Ratner Biomaterials Research Laboratory, UW Seattle
volunteer.summary: Research in scaffold design for vascular tissue engineering.
highlights: Training to operate a Kloé Dilase SLA 3D printer; prepare PDMS and photoreactive resin vats, run sensitivity tests, and print microscopic structures for bioengineering research.
Formulating novel printable biocompatible resins using photopolymerization of biopolymeric materials; troubleshoot material property challenges with iterative design.
Design 40-micron porous lattice microstructures in Onshape (truncated octahedron, rhombic dodecahedron, gyroid); collaborate with PhD students and faculty on printability and functional design.
Learning parametric modelling to increase scaffold design capabilities for vascularization research and arterial graft compliance.
Design and execute materials strength tests for a transtibial amputation prosthetic for pediatric patients; interpret results against international ISO standards.
Create CAD prototypes and 3D-printed PLA testing setups for the prototyping sub-team.
Navigated funding constraints to meet all required test specifications; contributed to HIC competition submission.
Support the business and project-management side of engineering in addition to technical work.

volunteer.organization: Virginia Mason Medical Center – Vascular Surgery
highlights: Provide direct patient interaction in an active clinical environment; assist with patient transport and prioritize genuine human connection beyond task-based care.
Follow PPE and infection-control protocols including room sanitization; completed code response training.
Observe transplant evaluations, rounding, and direct patient care in the ICU and dialysis clinic from the provider perspective.
Bring an informed patient lens as a kidney transplant recipient, deepening understanding of care for patients with ESRD and CKD.
Reading complex literature on kidney transplant immunology and clinical pathophysiology of renal disorders.
